title: Detect duplicate card swipes within two minutes
businessContext: Customers keep raising duplicate_processing disputes: a terminal retries an authorisation and the card is charged twice for the same amount at the same merchant within seconds. Clara wants to start refunding these proactively. As a first step she needs every suspected duplicate swipe of Q2 2026 so the team can size the problem before automating it.
requirements: Consider purchases (transaction_type = 'purchase') with status settled or authorized and a mapped merchant (merchant_id is not null).
For each such purchase, look at the previous purchase on the same card, at the same merchant, for the same amount and currency, ordered by created_at and then transaction_id.
Flag the purchase as a duplicate when that previous purchase happened at most 120 seconds earlier.

Report duplicates whose own created_at falls in Q2 2026 (2026-04-01 00:00 UTC inclusive to 2026-07-01 00:00 UTC exclusive), with the original and duplicate transaction ids and the number of whole seconds between them.
acceptanceCriteria: Columns are card_id, merchant_id, amount, currency, original_transaction_id, duplicate_transaction_id and seconds_apart, in that order.
seconds_apart is an integer between 0 and 120.
Each duplicate transaction appears once, paired with the purchase immediately before it.
referenceSql:
WITH candidates AS (
  SELECT transaction_id,
         card_id,
         merchant_id,
         amount,
         currency,
         created_at,
         LAG(transaction_id) OVER w AS previous_transaction_id,
         LAG(created_at) OVER w AS previous_created_at
  FROM fintech.transactions
  WHERE status IN ('settled', 'authorized')
    AND transaction_type = 'purchase'
    AND merchant_id IS NOT NULL
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY card_id, merchant_id, amount, currency ORDER BY created_at, transaction_id)
)
SELECT card_id,
       merchant_id,
       amount,
       currency,
       previous_transaction_id AS original_transaction_id,
       transaction_id AS duplicate_transaction_id,
       EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM created_at - previous_created_at)::integer AS seconds_apart
FROM candidates
WHERE previous_transaction_id IS NOT NULL
  AND created_at - previous_created_at <= INTERVAL '2 minutes'
  AND created_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-04-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND created_at < TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-01 00:00:00+00'
ORDER BY duplicate_transaction_id;
hints: Partition a window by card_id, merchant_id, amount and currency so that only identical swipes are compared.
LAG(transaction_id) and LAG(created_at) give you the previous swipe in the partition; compare the timestamps with an interval.
Apply the Q2 filter after the window is computed so a duplicate on 1 April can still find an original from 31 March.
explanation: LAG over a partition of identical card, merchant, amount and currency pairs each swipe with the one just before it, which is cheaper and easier to reason about than a self join. Filtering the time window after the LAG keeps originals that sit just before the period, and EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM interval) turns the gap into seconds.
